Recap (what we covered)

- Options for auth: API keys (recommended for server-to-server) vs OAuth (user-scoped flows).
- Routing: per-region routing + fallback to a compatible model if dedicated pool is constrained.
- Structured output/tool calling: brief on function-calling patterns and output envelopes.
- Embeddings / reranker: suggestion to upsert document IDs for idempotency and keep embedding version pinned.
- Throttling & retries: high-level best practices; Rishi will follow up with a concrete retry/backoff/playbook.

1) Can you confirm whether you want API-keys (server-side) or OAuth for initial integration? We recommend API keys for server processes + scoped keys for per-service separation.
2) Please share a rough traffic profile for peak windows (RPS, typical payload sizes / sequence lengths). This will let us size quotas and suggest burst policies.
3) Schedule a 60-min architecture deep-dive with Rishi next week to go over token-level throttles, idempotency and embedding lifecycle.

Hi Caroline — following up from the demo with a practical integration playbook focused on auth, throttling, retries and idempotency. Dropping implementation-level notes you can share with your engineering team.

Auth
- For server-to-server and batch jobs: API keys (scoped per-service). Use short-lived keys rotated via your secret manager and map to a customer id in headers.
- For user-facing flows requiring delegated permissions: OAuth 2.0 with PKCE.
- Header recommendations: Authorization: Bearer <token> and include X-Redwood-Client: <service-name> for routing/observability.

Request IDs & Idempotency
- Include X-Request-ID (UUID v4) on every request for tracing. Redwood surfaces these in Console logs for faster triage.
- For mutating operations (upserts, inference jobs that produce DB side-effects): include Idempotency-Key header (UUID) that your client generates and persists until the operation is confirmed. Server will dedupe within a 24-hour window.

429 / Throttling / Quotas (recommended playbook)
- Return behavior: respect server Retry-After (seconds) when provided. If no Retry-After, client should use exponential backoff with full jitter.
- Backoff params (suggested): initial=200ms, factor=2, max_backoff=10000ms, max_attempts=5. Add full jitter: sleep = random(0, backoff).
- Idempotency + retries: only retry non-idempotent endpoints if Idempotency-Key was supplied.
- Client-side rate limiting: implement a token-bucket with capacity=burst_size (choose based on your SLA), refill rate = sustainable_rps. This prevents thundering herd during failovers.
- Circuit breaker: open after 20 consecutive 5xx/429s for 30s, then half-open with a small probe.

Routing & Model variants
- Include X-Region in requests if you want hard-region routing. If omitted, we route by policy (latency/cost).
- Use model pins for consistency (e.g., model: 'redwood-text-xxl:v1.3'). Fallbacks use compatible variants with lower throughput/cost.

Embeddings & Reranker notes
- Upsert documents with stable external IDs to guarantee idempotency for embedding storage.
- Pin embedding model versions in calls to avoid drift; store model_version on your vector rows.
- For reranking: run a coarse embedding similarity pass, then send top-K candidates to the reranker (avoid doing full-rerank across all documents).
- Batch embeddings (up to 256 items) but keep payload size limits in mind. Use per-batch request IDs for tracing.

Code snippet (pseudocode):
- headers = { 'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + env.REDWOOD_KEY, 'X-Request-ID': uuid4(), 'Idempotency-Key': uuid4() }
- response = client.generate(payload, headers=headers)
- if response.status == 429: wait(retry_after or backoff_with_jitter()) and retry (up to attempts)

I'll attach an architecture sketch showing where the token-bucket and retry layer live in your stack (attached). Happy to walk through this on the deep-dive.

Thanks Marissa and Rishi — this is helpful. A few clarifying Qs from our side so we can prep for the deep-dive:

1) Quotas: our busiest window is market open (09:30-09:45 ET) where bursts spike ~3.5x baseline for ~3 minutes. We need guidance for per-tenant burst quotas vs global pool. Can Redwood enforce per-tenant token-bucket limits?

2) Retry semantics: you mention server dedupe for idempotency keys within 24h — what happens if a client restarts and loses local key state? Any server-side patterns to help (e.g., operation status APIs)?

3) Embeddings: we plan to upsert ~10k docs initially, and then incremental updates. Recommend a pattern to migrate embeddings if model version changes.

4) Security/compliance: we use a VPC peering for private deployments. Is there any special handling for rate-limiting metrics in Private mode?

We are available for a follow-up Tue 20th 11am ET (8am PT) or Wed 21st 2pm ET.

—Caroline Park

Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: SDK auth, throttling & retry playbook

Caroline — great questions, answered inline and proposing concrete next steps / mutual action items.

1) Quotas & bursts
- Yes, Redwood supports per-tenant token-bucket limits on Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we can provision per-customer soft quotas + hard global pool enforcement. For your peak: propose a per-tenant burst allowance = baseline_rps * 4 for 120s, with a throttle to baseline after. We can iterate on numbers in the deep-dive.

2) Retry / idempotency durability
- If a client loses local key state: use our operation-status endpoint to check the last known result for a given client-generated request-id. We also support optional server-side persistent idempotency keys (opt-in) for longer windows — this is something we can scope in SOW.

3) Embedding model migrations
- Recommended pattern: upsert new embedding vector column (model_v2_vector) while keeping model_v1_vector until validated. Run A/B reranking on a subset of traffic. We'll provide scripts for bulk re-embed and backfill.

4) Private/VPC mode metrics
- In Private deployments we still emit the same throttling telemetry to your Console; metrics are service-local and can be exported to your Prometheus. No behavioral difference in enforcement.

Mutual action plan (proposed)
- 1) Deep-dive architecture call (60m) with Rishi + Finlytics eng — Tue 20 Jan 11:00 ET (we confirmed on your availability).
- 2) Rishi to produce an integration checklist and a retry/playbook doc (target: Thu 22 Jan).
- 3) Redwood to provide SOW draft for Dedicated pool + SLA exception for market-open bursts (attached).
- 4) Post-call: Finlytics to provide traffic histogram + a list of endpoints that will be mutating (for idempotency planning).
